findings.claim: Narrowed but still open. O1's touches now cover verbs.py, check_verbs.py, judge.py, sections.py, instructions.py, check_instructions.py, ui.py, ui.html, the manifesto and overview.md. They still leave out mcp_server.py, where agents read the dropped verbs. Its server INSTRUCTIONS (line 50) tell agents that results and instructions name CLI verbs like `kmaudit claims submit - --path NAMESPACE`, which stops being true once instructions.py names the tools. Every tool description ends 'as `kmaudit claims todo --json`' (lines 141 to 304), naming a command that will exit 2. The touches also leave out models.py (lines 76 to 83) and check_store.py (lines 32 and 54), whose Field descriptions ('The claim id that kmaudit checks todo gave') land in the answer schema the todo tools hand to agents. coverage.py:113 ('run kmaudit checks run') and the docstrings in anchors.py, feedback.py, __init__.py and settings.py name dropped verbs too. The plan's own test, that no string in kmaudit's source names a dropped verb as a command, will fail on these files, so the build must change files O1 does not list. plan.split reads touches. Add at least mcp_server.py, models.py, check_store.py and coverage.py, or say which of these strings the test exempts.

The operator chose a 'Rerun stale checks' button backed by POST /api/rerun, which calls the same function as the MCP checks_run tool (check_verbs.run). The plan states it and O1's checked-by tests it. ui.py already serves POSTs (/api/feedback, /api/opinion) from a ThreadingHTTPServer, so a rerun that takes minutes does not block the page's other requests.

The plan now names the CLI-only behaviours whose tests go (reading answers from a file or stdin, the counts claims todo prints, the --help walk, the checks run exit codes, the refusal outside a git repository, the CLI-against-MCP comparisons). It keeps every other behaviour through the MCP tools or the Python functions, and the build notes list each deleted test.
